segments.t: 他们三人站在后走廊一面巨大的木书架前。格雷厄姆卷起袖子，亚瑟把那些沾满灰尘的旧书叠在地板上。如果你准备好了，让我们按下播放键，开始进入这一集。
Is it true? Is there really a secret room behind my kitchen wall?
Help me stack these big green books on the chair, Tessa.
Take the top shelf first so the wood becomes light.
These travel books are older than both of us, Hannah!
That is the last shelf. Ready to pull on three, Graham?
One, two, three... slide the left side toward me!
Look behind the wood! White paint and a brass keyhole!
A real door, hidden right here in the hallway!
Let us try the big key from the cedar box.
Does it turn, Graham?
One firm turn to the right... and the latch is open!
Lift the handle first, just like the front door!
现在，让我们仔细听听每一句对话。
Is it true? Is there really a secret room behind my kitchen wall?
‘帮我把这些绿色的书叠在椅子上，格雷厄姆。’把书整齐地叠放起来的动作总是使用
Is it true?
这个词源于古诺斯语中关于干草堆的说法。
Help me stack these big green books on the chair, Tessa.
‘每一本书闻起来都像干燥的秋叶。’表示每一本独立的书时，我们说
Help me stack
总是搭配单数动词，因为它是逐一指代的。
Take the top shelf first so the wood becomes light.
‘那是因为这个走廊没有暖气。我们从来没碰过这些木板。’这里指的不是任何一块板子，而是书架上结实的横板：
becomes light
也就是那些搁板。
These travel books are older than both of us, Hannah!
‘好吧，上面的架子空了。拉住左边边缘，亚瑟。’当需要抓紧某物准备用力时，非常自然的表达是
older than both of us
这意味着紧紧握住。
That is the last shelf. Ready to pull on three, Graham?
‘一，二，三，拉！太重了，格雷厄姆，这根本推不动！’当我们尽力去推却推不动时，我们说
on three
搭配 not 表示一动也不动。
One, two, three... slide the left side toward me!
‘等一下。底部的木头卡在一块松动的地板上了。’当地板的一块木板松动时，我们称之为
toward me
这个词结合了 floor（地板）和 board（木板）。
Look behind the wood! White paint and a brass keyhole!
‘现在我明白了！这件家具很旧，但没有钉子！’
keyhole
这个词统称所有的桌椅柜子，它在英语中不可数，也没有复数形式。
A real door, hidden right here in the hallway!
‘看！你可以直接把这些空架子滑出来！’这里的直接滑动动作使用了
right here
就像把一个抽屉拉出来一样简单。
Let us try the big key from the cedar box.
‘哦，天哪。这里有灰尘，有些虫子，还有……一个铁把手。’
Let us try
是一声常见的温和惊叹，就像‘哎呀，天哪’。
Does it turn, Graham?
‘那个箭头不是指向墙上的门。它指向地板上的门！’在英语中，介词 on 和 in 的区别很明确：在墙面上用
One firm turn to the right... and the latch is open!
而如果要进入一个空间则用 in。
One firm turn
‘把这最后一块板子拉起来。门栓没有锁。’我们通过滑动来拉开地板上的活板门：
Lift the handle first, just like the front door!
这个动词生动地描述了动作的轨迹。
just like
‘我们真的找到了九号房间吗？’对于发自内心的深切感受，
Is it true? Is there really a secret room behind my kitchen wall?
Help me stack these big green books on the chair, Tessa.
Take the top shelf first so the wood becomes light.
These travel books are older than both of us, Hannah!
That is the last shelf. Ready to pull on three, Graham?
One, two, three... slide the left side toward me!
Look behind the wood! White paint and a brass keyhole!
A real door, hidden right here in the hallway!
Let us try the big key from the cedar box.
Does it turn, Graham?
One firm turn to the right... and the latch is open!
Lift the handle first, just like the front door!
给问句增添了真诚和急切的感觉。让我们不间断地再听一遍这个场景。
See you later!
